name: Lady Vey
text: The east wing stays locked. My husband's portraits do not care for visitors.

name: Ilse
text: The cellar holds nothing but apples and spiders.

name: Brann
text: I polish the silver every Tuesday, and every Tuesday one spoon is missing.

name: Doctor Hale
text: Children from the village sometimes cut across the lawn.

name: Ilse
text: I will read the cards for you at midnight, but you must not laugh, or they turn sour.

name: Brann
text: Lady Vey always wears long sleeves.

name: Doctor Hale
text: The old lord died of a weak heart. I signed the paper myself and I stand by it.

name: Ilse
text: The grey mare bites anyone who is not family.

name: Lady Vey
text: Call the gardener the Mole; he digs in places nobody asked him to dig.

name: Doctor Hale
text: That clock chimes at odd hours.

name: Brann
text: If the bell in the pantry rings by itself, you leave the room and you do not look back.

name: Lady Vey
text: The music box plays a tune nobody can name.

name: Ilse
text: My grandmother hid a letter behind the third stair, and I never had the courage to read it.

name: Brann
text: The doctor owes half the village money.

name: Doctor Hale
text: I will give you something to sleep, but only two drops. Three and you will not wake for a day.

name: Brann
text: The east wing smells of damp and old varnish.

name: Lady Vey
text: I promise the inheritance goes to whoever finds the key, not to whoever shouts loudest.

name: Ilse
text: The silver here is older than the house.

name: Brann
text: I served three masters in this house, and only the second one ever said thank you.

name: Lady Vey
text: Card reading is a peasant habit.

name: Ilse
text: The cook puts rosemary in everything to hide the taste of the well water.

name: Brann
text: The old lord climbed the tower stairs every night.

name: Doctor Hale
text: Burn my notebook if anything happens to me. Do not read it, just burn it.

name: Ilse
text: The gardener grows roses the colour of bruises.

name: Lady Vey
text: The chapel bell has been silent since the wedding, and I intend to keep it that way.

name: Doctor Hale
text: Pantry bells ring when the wind is in the flue.

name: Brann
text: Call me when the candles gutter green. That means the cellar door is open again.

name: Brann
text: The stairs creak worst near the landing.

name: Ilse
text: I swear I saw a child on the lawn at dawn, barefoot, holding a lantern without a flame.

name: Lady Vey
text: The doctor drinks more than he prescribes.

name: Doctor Hale
text: The scar on Lady Vey's wrist is older than her marriage. Ask her who gave it to her.

name: Brann
text: The family lawyer has not visited in years.

name: Lady Vey
text: You may borrow the grey mare, but if she comes back lame you will pay in blood or gold.

name: Ilse
text: Brann has been here longer than the furniture.

name: Brann
text: The clock in the hall runs eleven minutes slow, and nobody is allowed to correct it.

name: Doctor Hale
text: The well is deep and very cold.

name: Ilse
text: Wren, promise me you will open the music box only when I am in the room.

name: Lady Vey
text: The doctor writes in a cramped little hand.

name: Doctor Hale
text: The gardener paid me in seeds once. They grew into something with teeth.

name: Brann
text: The chapel roof leaks over the altar.

name: Wren
text: What did Ilse ask Wren to promise about the music box?

name: Brann
text: Give me a moment to remember.

name: Wren
text: What did Doctor Hale say grew from the gardener's seeds?

name: Ilse
text: I think I can recall that.

name: Wren
text: What did Lady Vey say about the east wing?

name: Doctor Hale
text: Let me think back on it.

name: Wren
text: How many drops did Doctor Hale say were safe?

name: Ilse
text: That was a while ago now.

name: Wren
text: What did Ilse swear she saw on the lawn?

name: Brann
text: Ask me again later if I get it wrong.

name: Wren
text: What did Doctor Hale say the old lord died of?

name: Ilse
text: Rain drums on the roof for a while.

name: Wren
text: Why did Ilse say the cook puts rosemary in everything?

name: Brann
text: I think I can recall that.

name: Wren
text: What did Brann say about the clock in the hall?

name: Lady Vey
text: Let me think back on it.

name: Wren
text: What did Ilse say her grandmother hid?

name: Brann
text: That was a while ago now.

name: Wren
text: What did Brann say green candle flames mean?

name: Lady Vey
text: Ask me again later if I get it wrong.

name: Wren
text: What condition did Ilse set for reading the cards?

name: Brann
text: Give me a moment to remember.

name: Wren
text: What did Brann say about the masters he served?

name: Lady Vey
text: A door creaks somewhere down the hall.

name: Wren
text: What were Lady Vey's terms for borrowing the grey mare?

name: Doctor Hale
text: Let me think back on it.

name: Wren
text: What exactly did Brann say to do when the pantry bell rings by itself?

name: Lady Vey
text: That was a while ago now.

name: Wren
text: What did Lady Vey say about the chapel bell?

name: Doctor Hale
text: Ask me again later if I get it wrong.

name: Wren
text: What did Brann say happens every Tuesday?

name: Lady Vey
text: Give me a moment to remember.

name: Wren
text: What did Lady Vey promise about the inheritance?

name: Doctor Hale
text: I think I can recall that.

name: Wren
text: What did Doctor Hale say about the scar on Lady Vey's wrist?

name: Ilse
text: Rain drums on the roof for a while.

name: Wren
text: What did Lady Vey call the gardener?

name: Doctor Hale
text: That was a while ago now.

name: Wren
text: What did Doctor Hale ask be done with his notebook?

name: Ilse
text: Ask me again later if I get it wrong.
